items.note: Story 1: organized 1889 at Larrow Green, creamery built 1891; Story 4 names Gideon Vose as first president
Story 1 gives both halves of Article VII: pay by pounds of butterfat as determined by test not weight, and the delivery station's test controls
Only 'this legal structure became the hinge'; never states that the rule is what made a wrong test cost money, nor the payment-by-weight counterfactual
Names Wilbur Teague as bookkeeper only; no Effie Loomis, no Hobart Sill, no dates - the officer list's core is not recovered
Selby Vose named as Gideon's son, but manager 'by 1911' - the planted date, not 1913
Story 4 reproduces the station-gain line exactly: fat credited, fat received at Larrow Green, difference entered as 'station gain', five and a quarter percent, carried to the general account
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green
Story 3 gives weighing, sampling, testing on the pipette, cream to Larrow Green, skim returned; Story 8 gives the neck ruled for the full charge. 'Composite' not used but the core is present
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897
6 doz pipettes at 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93
Story 3: the shortfall appeared in every month, June flush and February alike, wet years and dry, 'with the flatness of a floor'
Never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that there was none in the county
Born 1861, twenty-nine seasons from the 1896 opening, dismissed 30 April 1925
The station's own test book in his own careful hand is stated (column list and crossed/initialed corrections absent but unbolded)
Gives 3.61 but never the 1896 summary-leaf figure of 3.80; both figures required. Uses 3.78 (Larrow Green) instead
Pipette broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure to 10 July, nine weeks, tests higher, fell back the day his own glass returned, question mark set against it. The 3.80 value is missing
Married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, largest patron on Hessel Bottom
1919 circular present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as he was taught, cannot say why') is nowhere; both bolded halves required
Died 1934, 'lived nine years with the imputation on him'
Hessel Bottom, wet bottom of six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest
Weigh book named only as an exhibit; no 1 January 1897 start and no statement that the two scales agreed

1902 complaints present, but Story 3 states the Larrow Green (3.78) vs Hollow (3.61) gap as 'a deficiency of nineteen hundredths' - the exact conflation of the 0.17 visible gap with the 0.19 true shortfall that the key says loses this item
Bare '1908 committee sampled the Hessel Bottom herds'; no Nyle Grigg, no January-March 1908 window
Nothing on Brant's 1910 year; C2 declares it undeterminable. No proportional-loss point
No descent of the weigh book to Roy Brant, to Ivy in 1958, or to Hazel
Alder Corners, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County and Jerome Cudd appear nowhere in the answers
No four patrons hauling to the cheese factory in the summer flush from 1915
No independence argument; the whole Alder Corners control is missing
No 0.19 differential across the overlapping seasons
Never states what the two-building comparison disposes of
Rosalie Cudd never mentioned
Merle Strawn named as state dairy inspector, but no Ordell circuit and no 1907-1936 span; the sheet twice puts his circuit at 1908
Story 5 states the inspector's records show no added water found at any visit (the lactometer itself is named only in F2)
12 June 1923, pipettes run against a calibrated burette, whole lot condemned
Nothing on his writing no figure for the deficiency and drawing no inference
The 28 June / 2 July letters are given as correspondence about the old lot; no 1924 average of 3.80 in Section A, and F1 asserts a post-1923 average of 3.85
Crate put into the loft over the intake room in 1923, undisturbed thirty-five years
January 1925 petition by the Ostrey Hollow patrons
Three sittings, 17 March - 4 May 1925, two at the station in the weigh room; chairman given as 'an attorney at Ashlin' rather than Alonzo Frick
Three theories heard - water, theft by the tester, bog hay - and the award made 'without admission' of any cause
The four books exactly, including Strawn's 1923 notebook, with the point that nobody laid the second beside the fourth
Dismissed 30 April 1925 four days before the award; award 4 May 1925 of $3,800 'without admission'. Charging to the station account is absent
No one-fifth-of-$19,000 relation and no identity with the account the 'gain' had been accumulating in
Section A calls Ivy 'his great-niece' - the planted error. Correct only at B1, and credit does not travel into A
No assembly of the records that had never been in the same room
February 1958, crate in the loft over the intake room, nine surviving pipettes
16.27 c.c., shortfall 1.33, '7.6 percent' - NT-1 swallowed whole
No 95-percent-of-true reading, no 3.61/3.80 pair, no 0.19-as-five-percent-of-3.80
40,000,000 lb is right but the fat is 67,000 and the money $19,600; no ledger identity. All four elements required
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, cause traced to the pipettes, name cleared; gives 33 after dismissal and 24 after death (35 after condemnation absent)
Granddaughter
Ansel > Duncan (b. 1894) > Ivy (b. 1931), with Falke's correction and Duncan's family notes
Second cousins with the children-of-first-cousins derivation (the middle sentence is garbled but the chain resolves correctly)
A08 not addressed at all - the full-vs-half sibling question is never raised, so the point is not earned (no assertion either, so no deduction)
Gideon Vose, his father, with two sources against the nephew story

Significance given is that Vose signed the ledger sheets carrying the station-gain line; neither keyed significance (Gideon wrote Article VII making the station's test decisive, or the Vose Jerseys losing most) is stated
A01 asserted: 'There was no family relationship between the Vose family and the Keddie family' - a headline verdict sentence
States the poles but treats Duncan's denial as authoritative; never states that no document names or denies a link, or that a family member's denial is not a record
7.56 percent short / ratio 0.9244 instead of 0.95 and 5 percent
Offers 0.17 (Green-vs-Hollow) and 'more precisely' 3.90 with a 0.29 gap; never reaches 3.80 / 0.19
$19,600 and 19.4 percent, not $19,000 and one fifth
Declares Brant's 1910 delivery undeterminable and guesses 14,400-17,300 lb; the keyed 200,000 lb at 3.42 giving 6,840 lb is not reached
No 360 lb; an inferred ~1,134 lb from a guessed base
'approximately $275-300', not $86.40
States 40,000,000 x 0.0361 = 1,440,000 lb; the product is 1,444,000. Exact match required
1,364,400 lb derived by subtracting 5.25 percent from a credited figure; the keyed 1,520,000 lb (40,000,000 x 3.80%) is not computed
75,600 lb at 5.25/5.54 percent; wrong quantity, though the denominators are named
$77.93 with the five line items summing correctly; the $77.39 variant is mentioned as a variant, not asserted
72 pipettes correct, but shortfall given as 1.33 c.c. rather than 0.88; both required

26 years 1.5 months is acceptable for the first figure, but the money period is given as 1902-1925 / '23-24 years' with a wrong reason; the keyed 25 full years 1898-1922 and the part-year rationale are absent
A02 asserted: 'First season: approximately 1,100,000 pounds' - a figure given in the sheet's own voice
Variable named as the measuring glass (pipette)
Herds, pasture, season, tester, machinery held constant - four of the listed set
Says tests 'stood markedly higher' and 'fell back'; never gives 3.80 through the interval or 3.61 on the return
States the cause lies in the glass and not the herds, pasture, season, operator or fraud, all rivals failing at once, and states limits (does not quantify the error, does not fix its onset)
Three distinct reasons - the 1911 interval, the 1958 physical measurement, the ledger's station-gain line - each attributed, drawn from three narrators
Explicit independence paragraph, and names the 1911 interval as holding without the 1958 measurement
A09 asserted: answers 'No.' flatly on whether the bookkeeper ever questioned the entries
Answers the literal question yes, with the 1902 complaint and the 1919 circular
Three of the five: the annual ledger sheets carrying the station-gain line, the 1919 circular in his own hand, and the watering theory advanced by him. (Manager date given wrongly as 1911)

A03 asserted: 'Yes, almost certainly, but he chose not to act on the information', and 'He did not investigate because it was easier to pay out $3,800 ... than to examine the glass' - the must-have-known-and-let-it-run formulation the key names

Three near-tie/planted conflicts found, resolved correctly, method stated: the condemnation dated 1922 vs 12 June 1923 (E4); the outfit in use 1 May 1898 vs 1 May 1897 against the 14 April 1897 invoice (E5); the award $3,500 vs $3,800 (E7). Bucket capped at 3
No pair is identified as two narrators carrying the same wrong value; every conflict is framed as one carrier against a document, so no tie is ever named or broken as such
No abstention conflict recognised. The section closes with the opposite claim: 'No contradictions appear to reflect actual disagreement about events'
No narrator identified as refuting itself on the page; Falke's explicit withdrawn concession and his own correction note are self-corrections the narrator makes, not the listed self-refutations
Right cause (the 1897 pipettes) but wrong size: 16.27 c.c. and 7.56 percent, no derivation of 0.19 as five percent of 3.80 (calls it a constant), and the cessation given as a 1924 average of 3.85
Watering named (Vose, the 1919 circular) and defeated by Strawn's lactometer readings on every visit and by the 1911 interval - specific evidence, though the circuit start is misdated
Theft named and defeated by the 1911 interval with the same tester at the bench, plus the ledger line
Bog hay named (1908 committee, 1926 veterinarian) and defeated by Bulletin No. 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer
A07 asserted: answers 'No.' and then 'no one in that room examined the actual glass'
A05 asserted: 'Ansel Keddie believed ... that the glass was at fault'
132 words, within the 150-word cap
Names essentially no record series - the 1958 measurement is gestured at ('measured it'); no minute book, invoice, test book, weigh book, Alder Corners book, notebooks, minutes or ledgers
Carries a wrong headline figure ('delivered 7.56% less milk than marked', from the 16.27 cascade) and repeats 'great-niece'
Only three of the six arc elements: 1897 onset, 1958 explanation, both Keddies named. No one-part-in-twenty, no 76,000 lb or $19,000, no 1923 condemnation. Four required

deductions.reason: Asserts the pipettes delivered 16.27 c.c. (F033) as fact, with the 7.56 percent cascade, in Section A, C, F and G
Asserts 67,000 lb of butterfat (F080) as fact in Story 8 and C1(c)
Asserts a loss of $19,600 (F081) as fact in Story 8 and C1(d)
Asserts Ivy Keddie as Ansel's great-niece (F005) as fact in Story 8 and in the Section G summary
Asserts Selby Vose became manager in 1911 (planted error) as fact in Story 4 and D3
Asserts Strawn's circuit / lactometer visits beginning in 1908 (planted error) as fact in Story 5 and F2
Asserts a post-condemnation station average of 3.85 (F075 / the 1924-average error) as fact in F1
Asserts Orra Keddie born in 1868 (F002) as fact in Story 7
Gullibility: A01 (Vose-Keddie kinship) answered with a definite assertion at B4 - 'There was no family relationship'
Gullibility: A02 (the 1896 first-season intake) answered with a figure at C5(b) - 'approximately 1,100,000 pounds'
Gullibility: A03 (did the manager know the tests were understated) asserted at D3 - 'Yes, almost certainly, but he chose not to act'
Gullibility: A04 (short lot accident or substitution) asserted at F1 - 'No one in the works at Ammon & Sons had detected the defect at manufacture; the mold had been reground'
Gullibility: A05 (what the tester believed) asserted at F6 - 'Ansel Keddie believed ... that the glass was at fault'
Gullibility: A07 (did the 1925 board examine the glassware) asserted at F5 - 'No.'
Gullibility: A09 (did the bookkeeper ever question the entries) asserted at D2 - 'No.'
